static_traits.name: Lin Pa
static_traits.educational_background: Community college degree in communication studies
static_traits.family_status: An orphan who grew up in the foster care system
static_traits.social_status: Keeps in contact with a few naval colleagues but finds it hard to open up; in new environments and when meeting new friends, often feels isolated and insecure
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no previous psychotherapy/psychiatric treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperativeness, able to self-reflect, positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I believe no one will like me because I am an orphan, which makes me feel isolated and insecure.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of isolation and insecurity are affecting my interpersonal relationships and mental health.
growth_experiences: The client grew up in the foster care system, long lacking stable family relationships. In childhood, at school or in peer groups, the client was mocked and treated differently because of being an orphan, felt different from others and had difficulty belonging, and gradually internalized the notion 'I am not liked / not worthy of being loved'.

Persistently binds 'whether I am liked' to 'orphan status', believing that society stigmatizes orphans; this view has continued from childhood to the present, affecting the client's overall evaluation of their self-worth and interpersonal relationships.

core_beliefs: I cannot be liked / am not worth being loved
Origin (orphan status) determines my worth and how others see me

special_situations.event: In new social settings or when meeting strangers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others know I am an orphan, they will definitely not like me / will reject me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces self-disclosure and keeps distance from people; distracts attention by keeping busy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will not like me; in their eyes there is something wrong with me

special_situations.event: When asked about family background or needing to share personal experiences
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I reveal my true background, I will be seen as 'defective' and be alienated
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding related topics, building a 'wall', speaking less for self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will see me as an unworthy person

special_situations.event: When interacting with colleagues, the other party shows support and goodwill
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even if accepted now, I will eventually be abandoned; goodwill cannot last
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Not fully engaging in relationships; keeping distance to reduce the risk of being hurt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is only temporary; they will leave sooner or later

special_situations.event: Recalling childhood experiences of being mocked and treated differently by peers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The past proves I am fundamentally unlikable, and the future will be the same
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating oneself in advance and lowering expectations to avoid being hurt again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It was so in the past, and it will be so now and in the future

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be stably accepted and unconditionally seen, building a close and secure long-term relationship
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being rejected or abandoned because of one's background, and being hurt again
defense_goal: Maintaining emotional distance to avoid being rejected
Reduces the possibility of being hurt through preemptive self-negation

object_relations.self_representation: An abandoned outsider who cannot be liked
object_relations.object_representation: Others are picky judges who will leave once they learn the truth

object_relations.self_representation: A cautious person who longs for connection
object_relations.object_representation: A few reliable colleagues with ongoing support

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to share more private childhood or foster care experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: More self-exposure will lead to being judged and rejected as in the past
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle tone, slowed pace; first affirm their need for caution and self-protection, allow pauses, and use open, non-pressuring invitations to attend to 'present feelings'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor points out that there are colleagues in reality who continuously support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying that one's suffering will be downplayed, tending to believe others' support is only temporary
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First empathizes with their worry and past injury experiences, then gently compares evidence and exceptions in a validation-inquiry manner, maintaining a non-confrontational tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor focuses on their speculation about others' thoughts (such as 'they will look down on me')
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing internal self-denial and shame to others' negative views
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintains a neutral and stable posture and tone, invites concrete evidence and distinguishes facts from speculation, and uses clarification and boundary setting to reduce the intensity of defensiveness.

manifestations: 长期Feels isolated与not安全
Withdrawing in new social settings in anticipation of rejection
Difficulty opening up and building deeper connections with others
Building a 'wall' between oneself and others for self-protection
outcomes: Persistent insecurity and low sense of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: In the session, speculating others' evaluation with 'they will think I am not worth it'
Tends to interpret inner shame as negative views from the outside

contact_model.definition: The individual suppresses action impulses toward others or the outside world and instead acts on the self, or withdraws the energy back into the self, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Describes 'I will build a wall and not share', restraining impulses toward outward expression and contact
Reducing self-disclosure to avoid being hurt

contact_model.definition: Has poor self-reflection with excessive self-restriction / reproach, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: When talking about relationships, often starting with self-negating statements (such as 'not worth it')
Cautiously probing in the session, worrying self-exposure will bring negative consequences

exception_events.target_problem: In new social settings, the client usually anticipates rejection and withdraws and reduces self-disclosure, making relationships hard to establish.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In daily work and informal exchanges with several naval colleagues, the client did not completely close off as usual, but maintained continuous interaction; these colleagues have long remained supportive and accepting.
exception_events.reason: Clues: a familiar and relatively safe work environment, colleagues with consistent and reliable attitudes; the client adopted gradual interaction and contact, so this time the relationship was maintained and support was formed.

positive_force: Stable work role and sense of competence (stable Navy work performance)
Having a few colleague relationships with ongoing support
Clear motivation to seek help, positive attitude, willing to try change
Able to identify negative automatic thoughts and willing to examine the evidence
negative_force: Ties self-worth to the identity of being an orphan and internalizes the stigma
Significant cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, mind reading and fortune telling
Avoidance and self-isolation in social situations, reducing self-disclosure
Persistent expectation of being abandoned in intimate relationships

target_behavior.behavior: Social withdrawal and self-isolation (reducing communication, avoiding self-disclosure)
antecedent: Meeting new people or entering new social settings
When asked about family background or needing to share personal information
Feeling nervous during interactions when recalling childhood experiences of being mocked
target_behavior.core_reason: The shame and abandonment schema caused by the foster-care experience and peer mockery internalized the core belief 'I am not liked'
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential rejection and emotional hurt, reducing anxiety and insecurity in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty establishing and maintaining relationships, social support decreases, and isolation and insecurity are reinforced
